column28: Daily Workflows

Solo founders, freelancers, and solopreneurs already talk through their problems to themselves, to a notes app, to a friend who doesn't understand the work. That existing habit produces no structure, no accountability, and no memory. They can't afford a coach, their close network doesn't understand startup pressure, and AI tools just validate whatever they say. Indecision is the single most expensive thing a founder does: every stuck loop is a delayed hire, a missed bet, a week lost.

Voice is the right medium because founders think out loud. When you type, you edit yourself. The polished version comes out. When you talk, the unfiltered version comes out: the real confusion, the thing you didn't know you were avoiding until you said it. DeLoop captures that raw ramble, reads between the lines to find what actually matters, asks the question that cuts through and builds a memory across every session so each call is sharper than the last.

Metric: Loop closure rate, the percentage of identified open loops closed within a 7-day window supported by commitment follow-through rate across sessions. A founder typically carries 8–12 unresolved loops simultaneously. Deloop targets closing 60%+ within the week and surfacing accountability in 100% of return calls.

Yes. I've developed a workflow while building a production AI application that keeps development fast without letting AI context become messy.

Some of the practices I use include:

Starting a fresh agent/session for each feature or task instead of accumulating unrelated context.
Using different models based on the task instead of always using the most capable (and expensive) frontier model.
Running multiple agents in parallel—for example, having one agent actively implementing a feature while another plans the next one. Once implementation is finished, the next feature already has a detailed plan, so there's minimal idle time and no overlap between agents.
Maintaining project-specific documentation (such as AGENTS.md) and reusable Skills so agents have consistent project context instead of re-explaining conventions each session.
Keeping prompts focused and scoped so context windows stay clean, responses remain predictable, and token usage stays efficient.

It isn't about a single clever prompt—it's about treating AI agents as collaborators with well-defined responsibilities and workflows that scale to a production codebase.
